goal.sl: Šteješ in poveš števila do tisoč (thirteen in thirty narazen, twenty-one, a hundred and five), vprašaš How many …? ter poveš starost, razdalje in cene.
goal.de: Du zählst und sagst Zahlen bis tausend (thirteen und thirty auseinander, twenty-one, a hundred and five), fragst How many …? und sagst Alter, Entfernungen und Preise.
goal.it: Conti e dici i numeri fino a mille (thirteen e thirty distinti, twenty-one, a hundred and five), chiedi How many …? e dici età, distanze e prezzi.
goal.en: You can count and say numbers up to a thousand (thirteen and thirty apart, twenty-one, a hundred and five), ask How many …?, and say ages, distances and prices.

say.sl: Štej z mano: **one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten** (ena do deset). Nič je **zero**, v telefonski številki pa **oh**: **oh one seven …** Pazi na **four** in **eight**: zvenita kot *for* in *ate*, pišeta pa se **four** in **eight**.
say.de: Zähl mit mir: **one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten** (eins bis zehn). Null ist **zero**, in einer Telefonnummer **oh**: **oh one seven …** Achte auf **four** und **eight**: sie klingen wie *for* und *ate*, geschrieben werden sie **four** und **eight**.
say.it: Conta con me: **one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten** (da uno a dieci). Lo zero è **zero**, in un numero di telefono **oh**: **oh one seven …** Attenzione a **four** e **eight**: suonano come *for* e *ate*, ma si scrivono **four** e **eight**.
say.en: Count with me: **one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten**. Nought is **zero**, and in a phone number **oh**: **oh one seven …** Watch **four** and **eight**: they sound like *for* and *ate*, but are spelt **four** and **eight**.

examples.sl: Gospod Tyson ima deset vreč ovsa.
examples.de: Mr Tyson hat zehn Säcke Hafer.
examples.it: Il signor Tyson ha dieci sacchi d'avena.

say.sl: Nato **eleven** in **twelve** (enajst, dvanajst), ki imata svoje besede. Od 13 do 19 se končajo na **-teen**: **thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen**, nato **twenty** (dvajset). Pazi na **thirteen** in **fifteen**: thir-, fif-, nikoli *threeteen* ali *fiveteen*; **eighteen** ima en t.
say.de: Dann **eleven** und **twelve** (elf, zwölf), eigene Wörter. Von 13 bis 19 enden sie auf **-teen**: **thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen**, dann **twenty** (zwanzig). Achte auf **thirteen** und **fifteen**: thir-, fif-, nie *threeteen* oder *fiveteen*; **eighteen** hat ein t.
say.it: Poi **eleven** e **twelve** (undici, dodici), parole a sé. Da 13 a 19 finiscono in **-teen**: **thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen**, poi **twenty** (venti). Attenzione a **thirteen** e **fifteen**: thir-, fif-, mai *threeteen* o *fiveteen*; **eighteen** ha una t sola.
say.en: Then **eleven** and **twelve**, words of their own. From 13 to 19 they end in **-teen**: **thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen**, then **twenty**. Watch **thirteen** and **fifteen**: thir-, fif-, never *threeteen* or *fiveteen*; **eighteen** has one t.

examples.en: Fifteen lambs are on the fell.

say.sl: Desetice se končajo na **-ty**: **twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety**. **forty** (štirideset) je brez u (a **four**, **fourteen**). **thirty** (trideset) naglasiš spredaj, **thirteen** (trinajst) zadaj, da te slišijo prav.
say.de: Die Zehner enden auf **-ty**: **twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety**. **forty** (vierzig) hat kein u (aber **four**, **fourteen**). **thirty** (dreißig) betonst du vorn, **thirteen** (dreizehn) hinten, damit man hört, welche du meinst.
say.it: Le decine finiscono in **-ty**: **twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety**. **forty** (quaranta) non ha la u (ma **four**, **fourteen**). **thirty** (trenta) ha l'accento davanti, **thirteen** (tredici) in fondo, così si capisce quale dici.
say.en: The tens end in **-ty**: **twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety**. **forty** has no u (but **four**, **fourteen**). Say **thirty** with the stress at the front and **thirteen** with it at the end, so people hear which one you mean.

say.sl: Od 21 do 99 je drugače kot v slovenščini najprej desetica, nato enica, z vezajem: **twenty-one** (enaindvajset), **thirty-five**, **seventy-four**, **ninety-nine**. Vprašaš **How many …?** (koliko), samostalnik za njim je v množini: **How many lambs? — Twenty-two.** (Koliko jagnjet? — Dvaindvajset.) Starost gre z be: **Auntie Edna is seventy-four.** (Teta Edna ima štiriinsedemdeset let.)
say.de: Von 21 bis 99 kommt anders als im Deutschen der Zehner zuerst, dann der Einer, mit Bindestrich: **twenty-one** (einundzwanzig), **thirty-five**, **seventy-four**, **ninety-nine**. Du fragst **How many …?** (wie viele), das Nomen danach steht im Plural: **How many lambs? — Twenty-two.** (Wie viele Lämmer? — Zweiundzwanzig.) Das Alter mit be: **Auntie Edna is seventy-four.** (Tante Edna ist vierundsiebzig.)
say.it: Da 21 a 99 prima la decina e poi l'unità, come in italiano, ma con il trattino: **twenty-one** (ventuno), **thirty-five**, **seventy-four**, **ninety-nine**. Chiedi **How many …?** (quanti), e il nome dopo è al plurale: **How many lambs? — Twenty-two.** (Quanti agnelli? — Ventidue.) L'età va con be: **Auntie Edna is seventy-four.** (Zia Edna ha settantaquattro anni.)
say.en: From 21 to 99 the ten comes first and the one after it, with a hyphen: **twenty-one**, **thirty-five**, **seventy-four**, **ninety-nine**. Ask **How many …?**, and the noun after it is plural: **How many lambs? — Twenty-two.** Age takes be: **Auntie Edna is seventy-four.**

examples.it: Il vecchio Wilf ha ottantaquattro anni.

say.sl: **a hundred** ali **one hundred** (sto), **a thousand** (tisoč, pisano 1,000). Britanska angleščina reče za stoticami **and**: **a hundred and five** (sto pet), **two hundred and forty** (dvesto štirideset). Za številom **hundred** ne dobi -s: **three hundred sheep** (tristo ovc). Cene: £3.50 je **three pounds fifty** (tri funte petdeset).
say.de: **a hundred** oder **one hundred** (hundert), **a thousand** (tausend, geschrieben 1,000). Britisches Englisch sagt nach den Hundertern **and**: **a hundred and five** (hundertfünf), **two hundred and forty** (zweihundertvierzig). Nach einer Zahl bekommt **hundred** kein -s: **three hundred sheep** (dreihundert Schafe). Preise: £3.50 ist **three pounds fifty** (drei Pfund fünfzig).
say.it: **a hundred** o **one hundred** (cento), **a thousand** (mille, scritto 1,000). L'inglese britannico dice **and** dopo le centinaia: **a hundred and five** (centocinque), **two hundred and forty** (duecentoquaranta). Dopo un numero **hundred** non prende la -s: **three hundred sheep** (trecento pecore). I prezzi: £3.50 è **three pounds fifty** (tre sterline e cinquanta).
say.en: **a hundred** or **one hundred** (100), **a thousand** (1,000). British English says **and** after the hundreds: **a hundred and five**, **two hundred and forty**. After a number, **hundred** takes no -s: **three hundred sheep**. Prices: £3.50 is **three pounds fifty**.

exercises.text: Mr Tyson is busy with numbers today. He's got ___ (12) sacks of oats in the mill. Jack's got ___ (40) lambs on the fell. Granny Maggie's got ___ (24) eggs for the cakes. The church is ___ (500) years old. And Mr Tyson is ___ (68)!

translation.sl: Gospod Tyson je danes ves v številih. V mlinu ima dvanajst vreč ovsa. Jack ima na hribu štirideset jagnjet. Babica Maggie ima štiriindvajset jajc za kolače. Cerkev je stara petsto let. Gospod Tyson pa ima oseminšestdeset let!
translation.de: Mr Tyson ist heute mit Zahlen beschäftigt. Er hat zwölf Säcke Hafer in der Mühle. Jack hat vierzig Lämmer am Berg. Oma Maggie hat vierundzwanzig Eier für die Kuchen. Die Kirche ist fünfhundert Jahre alt. Und Mr Tyson ist achtundsechzig!
translation.it: Oggi il signor Tyson è alle prese con i numeri. Ha dodici sacchi d'avena nel mulino. Jack ha quaranta agnelli sul monte. Nonna Maggie ha ventiquattro uova per le torte. La chiesa ha cinquecento anni. E il signor Tyson ha sessantotto anni!
translation.en: Mr Tyson is busy with numbers today. He's got twelve sacks of oats in the mill. Jack's got forty lambs on the fell. Granny Maggie's got twenty-four eggs for the cakes. The church is five hundred years old. And Mr Tyson is sixty-eight!
